title: HC Mike LaFleur Postgame Press Conference | Week 6 vs. Los Angeles Rams
headline: Cardinals beat the Rams on a late Jacoby Brissett throw to Jalen Brooks; offense is moving the ball in long drives but lacks big plays and red-zone finish, and Bam Knight's absence was only cramping.
summary: LaFleur opened with injuries: Bam Knight kept cramping up (nothing more serious), and Walter Nolen had a right ankle issue with no further detail. He called the win a sign of resilience after two rough weeks, including a blown lead against the Giants and a 'total failure' last week that he put on himself. The offense had four drives of 10+ plays, with LaFleur saying the key was getting the first first down and staying in third-and-manageable, though the team is not hitting big plays and the red zone needs work, which he said he can help with through play calls and planning. He praised Jacoby Brissett for timing and accuracy all day and for his best throw at the end. The game-winning play featured Jalen Brooks, who made a play on third down after a similar route by another receiver (KB) fell short, and LaFleur said he trusted Brooks because of his daily work and mindset. He wants to start plugging Brooks in more in the red zone. The defense, under coordinator Nick, was aggressive with blitzes and situational looks against Stafford and led the league in fourth-down stops. Special teams were also called an edge, with the kickers making six field goals.

injuries.detail: Kept cramping up during the game, which explained his in-and-out playing time; nothing more serious mentioned.
Right ankle issue; LaFleur had no further information. (Roster lists Walter as Walter Nolen.)

signals.claim: Brooks will be worked into the red-zone offense more going forward.
signals.note: He made the game-winning play and the coach said he wants to plug him in the red zone, a possible target-share bump.
signals.quote: we start plugging them in in the red zone

signals.claim: Brissett continues to run the offense efficiently with timing and accuracy.
signals.note: Coach praised his accuracy and the sustained drives, which supports his stable starting role.
signals.quote: Jacoby was excellent all day in terms of timing and accuracy

signals.claim: Knight's in-and-out usage was due to cramping, not a significant injury.
signals.note: Cramping means no lasting injury concern, but his snaps were disrupted this week.
signals.quote: Bam just kept cramping up.

signals.claim: Nolen has a right ankle injury of unknown severity.
signals.note: Defensive lineman whose availability is uncertain; relevant only for IDP.
signals.quote: Walt had a right ankle.

topics.detail: Long drives and third-and-manageable situations, but no big plays and poor red-zone finishing; LaFleur takes responsibility for play design and calls. Used screens and tosses to attack the perimeter and make the defense back off.
Aggressive blitz-heavy plan from Nick against Stafford with new situational looks; the unit leads the league in defensive fourth-down stops.
Called an edge for the team; kickers made six field goals, and the kickoff return unit gave him confidence late.
After blowing a lead to the Giants and a failure last week, the team had tough conversations and bounced back; LaFleur calls it a one-week-at-a-time league.

title: Head Coach Kevin Stefanski Post-game Press Conference | Week 6 | Falcons vs. Bears
headline: Falcons fall flat at home to Chicago after a terrible start; Kendal Daniels' injury update is positive, Bijan got just 9 carries, and rookie Zachariah Branch's fumbles are a concern but he keeps his role.
summary: Stefanski opened with an injury update on Kendal Daniels, saying he had movement in his extremities on the field and that early reports are good after the medical staff got him off safely. He called the loss disappointing and said the team beat itself, especially with a slow start that he put on himself and the staff. Offensively the team had two three-and-outs early, both on long third downs against Dennis Allen's defense, and he said they need to install and execute the game plan better. Three turnovers, including two Zachariah Branch fumbles (one on a punt fielded inside the 10), hurt badly, though Stefanski said they are still counting on the rookie and will keep coaching him. He said Michael Penix Jr. is healthy enough and declined to evaluate his play, saying the whole offense needs to start faster. He acknowledged Bijan Robinson's light workload (4 first-half carries, 9 total) as a product of game flow and the poor start. The offense found rhythm in the fourth quarter with good pass protection, explosive plays and two two-point conversions while down 24, but it was not enough. He also credited Chicago's blitzing and screen game and said the team was 0-for-3 on fourth down.

injuries.detail: Was down on the field with an apparent serious injury; he had movement in his extremities and Stefanski said all reports so far are good, with no timeline given.
Stefanski said he is 'healthy enough' while playing quarterback, with no specifics on any ailment.

signals.claim: Branch remains someone the team will count on despite fumbling twice, including on a punt return.
signals.note: Ball security is a concern for his return duties, but the coach publicly backed him, so his role looks safe for now.
signals.quote: Zachariah is somebody that we're going to be counting on.

signals.claim: Bijan's light workload (9 carries) was due to game flow and the slow start, not a planned change in role.
signals.note: Volume should rebound in a more neutral game script, but he gave no commitment to more touches.
signals.quote: that's game flow, etc. I get that part.

signals.claim: Penix is healthy enough to play, but the coach declined to assess his performance.
signals.note: The quarterback appears to be dealing with some level of soreness and the offense's early struggles put pressure on him.
signals.quote: Mike's healthy enough.

topics.detail: Two early three-and-outs on long third downs, plus three turnovers and an 0-for-3 mark on fourth down, put the team in a big hole. Stefanski took responsibility for the poor game plan and execution.
Chicago's Dennis Allen blitzed effectively (defensive back Gordon cited) and used screens from all personnel groupings, which gave Atlanta trouble.
Pass protection held up and the offense produced explosive plays and two two-point conversions while down 24, but it was too late.
Aggressiveness depended on game situation, distance and play call, with the late decisions driven by needing multiple scores.
The team practiced with crowd noise and used a silent count at home as a precaution.

title: Jesse Minter Recaps Ravens' Road Loss to Browns
headline: Ravens' run game was shut down by Cleveland's aggressive front after the first drive; Derrick Henry's fumble was a costly turnover, but Minter backed his ball security and offered no lineup changes.
summary: Minter credited Cleveland and blamed the narrow loss on Baltimore's own mistakes: a fumble, a missed kick, and a red-zone penalty kept the Ravens from building a bigger lead in the second half. He said the team played well enough to separate and would look at itself and move on to next week. On Derrick Henry's fumble, he said nobody works harder on ball security, and he noted the defense failed to answer with a stop, which made the play bigger. He described Cleveland's front as aggressive: after a well-done first drive, the Browns jetted upfield and cut off angles on the zone run schemes. The Ravens could not sustain anything on the ground and need more answers against that kind of defense. He added that Cleveland also played tight, aggressive man coverage, which let them put an extra defender near the line, so the Browns defended both the run and the pass. On the late long catch where Nate Wiggins fell down, he gave credit to the opponent, said the team would check the tape, and said he thought the defense had bottled up the passing game most of the day. He gave no injury updates and no roster or depth-chart news.

signals.claim: Henry's fumble will not change his role; Minter publicly backed his ball security.
signals.note: Henry had a rushing struggle against an aggressive front plus a costly fumble, but the coach showed full confidence, so his workload should stay safe, though the run game may need adjustments.
signals.quote: Nobody works harder at ball security and does those things.

signals.claim: The team will review the tape of the play where Wiggins fell down on the long catch.
signals.note: This is a defensive play with little direct fantasy impact, but it may matter for opposing receivers facing Baltimore's secondary.
signals.quote: We'll look at the tape and see what it was.

topics.detail: Cleveland's aggressive front jetted upfield and cut off angles on Baltimore's zone run schemes after the first drive. The Ravens need more answers for that style of defense.
Self-inflicted errors (a fumble, a missed kick, a red-zone penalty) kept the game close. Minter said the team would look at itself and prepare for next week.
The Browns played tight, aggressive man coverage, which freed an extra defender near the line and stifled both the run and the pass.

title: Dave Canales on win vs. Eagles: 'The guys came together'
headline: Chuba Hubbard topped 120 rushing yards and Tommy Tremble scored twice in a versatile role, as Carolina won by 11 despite a franchise-record penalty total.
summary: Canales credited all three phases for the road win over the Eagles. The offense produced drives when needed, the defense got stops, and a late punt block by practice-squad call-up Tre Tyus was huge. He was blunt about the penalties, which he called outrageous and a franchise record. He wants cleaner hands, and he singled out linemen being downfield on screens as an obvious fix. He took the blame for the muddled end of the first half, saying he was indecisive on a potential go-for-it near the goal line and should have organized the team better so Bryce Young and the offense knew the plan. Chuba Hubbard got over 120 rushing yards against varied fronts from Eagles coordinator Vic Fangio, and Canales said he is running well right now. Tommy Tremble was used at fullback, on the perimeter and as a delay-block touchdown scorer, and Canales praised his toughness and versatility. Canales said Young took care of the ball, threw it away when needed and added yards with his legs, even in what was statistically his worst game of the season. He added that the defense's strong play let him be less aggressive on some fourth downs.

signals.claim: Hubbard's strong running will keep complementing the rest of the offense as the lead back.
signals.note: He topped 120 rushing yards against a varied Eagles front and the coach says he is running well, which supports a heavy workload.
signals.quote: he's running the ball really well right now

signals.claim: Tremble will keep being used in multiple ways, including fullback and on the perimeter.
signals.note: He scored two touchdowns and the staff is scheming him into varied roles, which raises his TD upside despite modest volume.
signals.quote: a little bit of fullback moving around, getting him on the perimeter

signals.claim: Young will keep playing a ball-secure, win-first style, using his legs and throwing the ball away when needed.
signals.note: He had 280 yards and a touchdown in what was statistically his worst game of the season, which points to a stable floor.
signals.quote: if he continues to play like this, he gives us a great chance

topics.detail: Carolina set a franchise record for penalties, mostly holding calls and linemen downfield on screens. Canales called them effort penalties and said he understood the calls, though he thought some on the other side were missed. The team will work on cleaning up its hands.

Canales owned the confusing finish to the first half, saying he was too indecisive on a potential go-for-it from about a yard and a half out. He would have preferred to break the huddle and try to draw the Eagles offside, then take a delay and punt.

Tre Tyus, a practice-squad call-up, blocked a late punt, which gave Carolina the ball at midfield after a three-and-out deep in its own territory. Canales also credited the other special teams players on the play.

A young defensive back, not clearly identified in the captions, had a strong game with several pass breakups and two penalties while playing press. Canales said he is fine with the penalties because the player is challenging receivers, though he wants cleaner hands. The reporter's question implied the secondary is adjusting to missing two players, but the coach did not address injuries.
Canales said the defense playing so well let him skip some fourth-down attempts he might otherwise have taken. He still went for the obvious ones.

Canales said Fangio's defense showed different looks that made the run game challenging. The offense stuck with it and found success, especially in the fourth quarter. He also noted a third-down design the coaches had worked on with Jalen Coker in recent weeks.

title: Ben Johnson proud of all 3 phases in win over Falcons | Press Conference
headline: Caleb Williams returned from injury and played well in a CHI win over ATL, Kyler Gordon was activated and delivered 3 sacks on a limited role, and Jackson's left hip needs a look before Thursday.
summary: Johnson praised the team's response after a rough prior week, saying all three phases showed their identity in the win in Atlanta. The defense swarmed Bijan Robinson, special teams produced a couple of fumble recoveries, and the offense held the ball for over 40 minutes. Caleb Williams and Kyler Gordon were the two returning players who gave the team a spark. Williams had a strong week of preparation, pushed to play, and found open receivers, including on key third-and-long throws early. Gordon was activated the morning before the game and had three sacks and two forced fumbles, but Chicago is deliberately limiting his role to make sure he is in good football shape. Johnson singled out Colston Loveland's catching in the red zone and said Luther Burden III made a good catch in tight coverage. He was frustrated by penalties, including an ejection for using the head, but said one bad game doesn't make a trend. He also said the team was managing the fourth quarter with a short week and a Thursday game in mind. Mr. Jackson has a left hip injury that will be evaluated Monday to determine his Thursday availability.

injuries.detail: Left hip injury; will be examined tomorrow to determine what it means for Thursday's game.
Activated the day before the game after missing time; played a limited role and was productive. Chicago wants to keep him on the right track.
Returned from his longest injury layoff and played in the win; received the game ball.

signals.claim: Williams is healthy enough to start and run the offense, and he is expected to keep playing going forward.
signals.note: His return from injury and strong performance restores confidence in the Bears' passing offense and its pass catchers.
signals.quote: he did a great job downloading the game plan

signals.claim: Gordon's role will be limited somewhat while he builds football shape, though he'll keep making impact plays as a nickel blitzer.
signals.note: Strong IDP production (3 sacks, 2 forced fumbles), but a deliberately limited snap count caps his ceiling.

signals.claim: Loveland is a trusted red-zone pass catcher and made a big play on the opening touchdown drive.
signals.note: Positive red-zone involvement and chemistry with Williams boost his fantasy outlook.
signals.quote: I thought Colston was was uh, catching that ball really well.

signals.claim: Burden is a reliable target who can win in tight coverage.
signals.note: Coach praised his catch in coverage, suggesting continued involvement in the passing game.
signals.quote: Luther had a good one in tight coverage as well.

signals.claim: Jackson's availability for Thursday will be determined after a Monday evaluation of his left hip.
signals.note: His status for the short-week game is uncertain, which matters for IDP.

topics.detail: Chicago plays Thursday, so the staff tried to thread the needle in the fourth quarter between winning and managing long-term health. An offensive fumble kept them from closing the game out as planned.
There was an ejection for using the head and several penalties. Johnson said the team needs to clean up its hands and awareness, but won't overreact to one poor game.
Johnson said this was the first complete team win of the season, with energy and confidence spreading from the sideline, and a good foundation to build on.
The Bears bottled up Bijan Robinson, whom Johnson called a dynamic MVP-race contender, while Atlanta's offense showed it can score quickly late.

title: Shane Steichen: Colts vs. Titans postgame
headline: Steichen says Daniel Jones is still the Colts' starter after a 26-20 loss to Tennessee, but the offense's turnovers and protection problems are unresolved; Anthony Gould left with a concussion and calf issue.
summary: Steichen called the 26-20 home loss to the Titans extremely disappointing and said the team has a lot to fix quickly. He blamed turnovers, a blocked punt, a long kick return, penalties (including pass interference calls) and a failure to score in the red zone or hold a lead. He said the defense played well in the first half. He explained Daniel Jones's interception as a Cover 2 corner sinking into the throwing window. He said he loves Jones and that the quarterback knows he has to play better, but he also said he has to coach better and that it's not on one guy. When asked directly, he confirmed Jones is the starting quarterback. He admitted the Colts struggled against Tennessee's blitz, with a lot of quarterback hits allowed, and said the team needs to generate its own pressure and protect better. Asked about his job security and possible staff changes, he said he's looking at everything but feels good about his staff. He said he hasn't talked to ownership about a vote of confidence. The Colts are 2-4 and face Minnesota next.

injuries.detail: Suffered a concussion and a sore calf during the game; no timeline given.
A player the captions call 'Rigo' had a foot injury but came back into the game; the name can't be confidently matched to the roster.

signals.claim: Daniel Jones remains the Colts' starting quarterback going into the Minnesota game.
signals.note: Jones keeps the job for now, but the turnovers, pressure and booing leave his leash uncertain and the offense's output risky.
signals.quote: Yes. He's our starting quarterback.

signals.note: A concussion plus a calf issue puts Gould's availability for Week 7 in question, which matters for the Colts' return and depth at receiver.

topics.detail: Steichen cited turnovers, a blocked punt and a big kick return as the main problems, and said the team will study the blocked punt closely this week.
The Colts allowed roughly a dozen quarterback hits against Tennessee's blitzes. Steichen said they need to pressure the quarterback and protect better, and he will review the tape.
Steichen said he is focused on getting the team ready, feels good about his staff and has not had vote-of-confidence conversations with ownership.
He said his tone with the team is 'pretty pissed off,' that preparation was clearly not good enough, and that the team needs to examine its process. He didn't blame the fans for booing.

title: Coen on Loss to Texans: “I’ve Got a Lot of Confidence in This Team.” | Press Conference
headline: Coen defended Brian Thomas Jr.'s involvement after the 34-31 loss, but a player who got no second-half snaps got only a noncommittal 'week to week' answer, and the run game was just serviceable.
summary: Coen called the 34-31 loss to Houston in London disappointing and not good enough, saying the Texans made too many plays and that the offense gave up sacks. He downplayed the pass-rush pressure and suggested the surface and venue favored the offense. He said getting Brian Thomas Jr. more involved early was part of the plan. He praised Thomas for making critical plays on both sides of the ball, including a late interception, and said he wants to keep feeding him, especially for yards after the catch. When asked whether he could keep confidence in a player who struggled and got no second-half snaps, he gave only a 'week to week' answer, saying guys have to step up and make plays. The identity of that player is not clear from the transcript. On the run game, he said the Texans' run defense is good and the yardage was below what he wanted, but the offense adjusted and Chris ran hard. He blamed some drops partly on the wet conditions and said he couldn't tell whether the late deep corner ball to Parker Washington was catchable. He cited penalties (a touchdown wiped out by a hold, a DPI before the half) and a substitution mistake on a fourth-and-one punt-safe situation. He said he has a lot of confidence in the team and won't change the process.

signals.claim: Thomas will keep getting targets and touches, including yards-after-catch opportunities, as the offense builds around him.
signals.note: Coen explicitly said he wants to keep getting Thomas the ball after an involved game, which supports his fantasy outlook.
signals.quote: We got to continue to get him the ball and keep building off of it

signals.claim: Rodriguez remains part of the rushing attack, though the team's run production was below expectations against a good run defense.
signals.note: Coen praised his effort but admitted the yardage fell short, so the efficiency outlook is mixed.
signals.quote: they ran really hard and gave us a chance at least to, to win it

signals.note: A late deep corner ball to Washington wasn't completed, and Coen couldn't tell if it was catchable, so there's no clear verdict on his role.

topics.detail: A holding call wiped out a touchdown and an interception followed two plays later. A DPI before the half set up Houston inside the three. Coen also admitted subbing off on a fourth-and-one when the unit should have stayed in punt safe.
Coen said the offense gave up sacks but didn't feel much duress, and that the wet conditions contributed to some drops. He said the team has to make those plays.

Coen said he has a lot of confidence in the team and won't change the process. He pointed to the team fighting back from 10-point deficits and getting a late field goal to tie, and said back-to-back close games are useful early tests.
Coen called the London experience first class and said the group handled it well. He was disappointed not to give the traveling fans a win.

title: Sean McVay, Matthew Stafford & Puka Nacua recap the Rams’ Week 6 loss to the Cardinals
headline: McVay offered nothing positive after the 18-16 loss to Arizona, with no player-specific fantasy news beyond a kicker injury and an unnamed player's knee injury with no update.
summary: McVay opened by saying the Rams will not win until they stop beating themselves. He cited unforced errors: a big kickoff return allowed, losing the kicker to injury during kickoff coverage, turnovers, and an offsides penalty on 4th-and-3. He said the defense did enough to keep the game close by holding Arizona to five field goals, but the offense did not give the team a chance, and he said he has to do a better job. He called the blitz problems a matter of execution, not of surprise, and said the team had chances to make Arizona pay. He did not know why the mistakes keep happening, saying 'a lot of different guys are taking their turn,' and he had no answers yet. He said the team's identity is still being figured out. He said the lack of a healthy kicker changed his late-second-quarter decision to run out the clock instead of going for it. He had no update on a player who hurt his knee. Stafford and Nacua echoed the 'execution' theme, citing third-and-long, Arizona's disguised looks, and falling behind the chains.

injuries.player: Kicker (name not given; Ethan kicked the extra point)
injuries.detail: The kicker was lost to injury during kickoff coverage, and 'Ethan' kicked the extra point with Stetson Bennett holding. McVay said that with a healthy kicker, he would have approached the end of the second quarter differently. No timeline was given.
Asked about a player, McVay said he had no update and only knew the player 'got his knee.' The player's name is not clear from the transcript.

topics.detail: McVay pointed to turnovers, negative plays, the 4th-and-3 offsides, a big kickoff return allowed, and the kicker's injury. He said the problem has been a recurring narrative this season and that he is responsible for fixing it.
McVay called the issues execution, not surprise, saying the Rams had chances to make the blitz pay and did not. The offense only found rhythm on the final touchdown drive.
McVay praised the defense for keeping the Rams in the game and holding Arizona to five field goals.
With no field goal operation available, the Rams played for a touchdown and ran out the clock late in the second quarter. The kicker's injury changed their approach.

McVay said the team is still figuring out its identity and denied that outside expectations are the issue. He said 'there's nothing positive that I can say about today' but that he still loves the group's fight.

title: Kellen Moore recaps win in New York | Saints-Giants Postgame | 2026 NFL Week 6
headline: Saints beat the Giants and head to Paris. Cesar Ruiz (knee) gets an MRI, Quincy Riley (neck) and Kool-Aid McKinstry (migraine) are minor concerns, and the three-back rotation stays.
summary: Kellen Moore was proud of the win on the road after a wild game. The Saints created four turnovers, gave one away, and rushed for 175 yards, which he called a key physicality goal. He said the run game took off in the second half because the team avoided penalties and negative plays and the runners ran hard. Cesar Ruiz left with a knee injury and will get an MRI before the team leaves for Paris. Quincy Riley had a neck issue late and Kool-Aid McKinstry had a migraine, but Moore said everyone else was good to go. Moore said he pulled a couple of sore starters after a 24-point deficit, and it backfired when the Giants kept scoring. He praised rookie-type contributor Jeremiah Wright's blocking and Martin Emerson's physical corner play. He confirmed the backfield is a three-man rotation with defined roles and complimented Alvin Kamara's timely plays. The team flies to Paris tonight for the first NFL game in France. Moore said the early arrival will help with acclimation and routine, and he has no concerns about the protests.

injuries.detail: Knee injury, did not finish the game. He will get an MRI as soon as possible before the team travels to Paris. Moore said he was moving around okay in the locker room.
Neck issue late in the game after colliding with Martin Emerson. Moore said 'I think we're okay.'
Left the game with a migraine plus an on-field issue (he also had a fumble). Moore said the team has to work through it.
Had the wind knocked out of him after colliding with Riley, then returned to the game. He has also been navigating an injury rotation.

signals.claim: Kamara will continue to share the backfield in a three-back rotation with defined roles.
signals.note: A committed three-way split caps his volume even though he made timely plays.
signals.quote: I thought he made some big plays, timely plays when we needed them.

signals.claim: Wright will keep contributing and playing, mainly as a physical blocker.
signals.note: A physical blocker earning trust could help the run game that produced 175 yards.
signals.quote: we feel like he can he can go contribute and play.

signals.claim: Emerson is finding his groove at corner after an injury rotation and is getting more involved in plays.
signals.note: A productive, physical corner (about seven tackles and two pass breakups or picks) helps the Saints' defense and IDP value.
signals.quote: I thought he took advantage of those opportunities.

signals.claim: Ruiz will get an MRI on his knee before the team goes to Paris.
signals.note: An offensive line injury could affect the run game and pass protection next week.
signals.quote: he'll get the MRI.

signals.claim: Riley's neck issue is not expected to be serious.
signals.note: Minor concern for the secondary depth.
signals.quote: I think we're okay.

signals.claim: McKinstry needs to work through the migraine issue before the next game.
signals.note: His availability is worth monitoring, especially after his fumble.
signals.quote: Kool-Aid had a little bit of a migraine thing going on.

topics.detail: Moore said that after a turnover made it a 24-point game, the team rested a couple of sore starters (it sounded like Erik McCoy and Tyler Shough). The Giants kept scoring, and he admitted it didn't work.
The Saints rushed for 175 yards, driven by physical play, few penalties and negative plays, and more rush attempts in the second half.
Four takeaways, including a forced fumble on special teams, plus a field goal late in the first half that sparked a strong middle eight minutes. The one giveaway was costly.
Moore called the kickoff unit special, saying it pins opponents inside the 25 almost every week. Chris Rumph had a big tackle.
Asked about a report that a player has two broken bones in his left hand, Moore said the player is battling but able to do everything.
The team flies tonight and arrives early to acclimate for the first NFL game in France. Moore said he feels great about the league's planning despite the protests.
After three straight losses, Moore said the team played with urgency and stuck together.

title: Postgame Press Conference: Coach John Harbaugh on loss to Saints
headline: Harbaugh is keeping the QB job open after the Saints loss: Jameis Winston was 'up and down' and J.J. McCarthy impressed in relief, while the RB room is still a four-man committee with no lead back.
summary: Harbaugh called the loss disappointing, with some good moments and long stretches of non-winning football. He said the run game was 'not very good' and 'not even close to good enough.' The defense was poor against the run, gave up too many quarterback scrambles, and had coverage lapses. He said the offense isn't hitting basic plays. He liked McCarthy's work in desperation time and praised his mobility as a big part of his skill set. He refused to name a starting QB going forward, saying it was only ten minutes after the game, but admitted the evaluation process 'starts right now.' He said he has no problem with Winston, who was up and down. On the backfield, he said he deliberately split snaps among four backs in the first half to find a hot hand. The second-half no-huddle and the deficit pushed the third-down backs onto the field, and one back (apparently Cam Skattebo) ended up with only six snaps without any runs called for him. Harbaugh said none of the backs has yet stepped up to be 'the back,' but that one will earn the job. He explained his late-game clock management (going for the two-minute warning, not running a rushed play) and called the next game at Houston huge.

signals.claim: McCarthy is in the mix for the starting QB job, which Harbaugh says is being evaluated starting immediately.
signals.note: A real QB competition with Winston raises McCarthy's stash value, and his mobility is a fantasy plus if he starts.

signals.claim: Winston's status as the starting QB is not guaranteed for the next game and is under evaluation.
signals.note: Harbaugh backed his competitiveness but wouldn't commit him as the starter, so his fantasy floor is shaky.
signals.quote: I love the way he competes. Love the way he fights.

signals.claim: No RB has claimed the lead job yet, and snaps will keep being split until one steps up.
signals.note: Skattebo had only six snaps and no designed runs, and the committee makes every Giants RB a risky fantasy start.
signals.quote: Somebody needs to step up and be the back.

signals.note: Harbaugh praised his deep catch during the comeback push, but it is a single-play compliment, not a role change.
signals.quote: That was awesome. I thought it was a great play.

topics.detail: Harbaugh would not name a starter right after the game, saying it's not up for discussion yet. He said the process of thinking about a change begins immediately. McCarthy's late-game snaps were mostly the regular no-huddle offense, not a special package.

Harbaugh said the run game was poor, and he admitted he doesn't love splitting snaps among four backs. The split was a deliberate attempt to find a hot hand. Being down by 24 moved the third-down backs into the game in the second half.
The defense is not stopping the run, is allowing too many quarterback scrambles, and had some coverage problems. Harbaugh said it needs to be much more consistent.
Harbaugh defended spiking the ball to get the two-minute warning rather than rushing a play that could have caused chaos. The plan was to score and go for two if they scored.
The end-of-first-half fumble and the failure to stop the Saints after halftime let them back into the game, contributing to a 17-point run.

title: Nick Sirianni Press Conference: October 18, 2026
headline: After a 25-14 loss and a fourth straight defeat, Sirianni says 'everything's on the table' for an offense that isn't scoring or running the ball. Tanner McKee got praise.
summary: Sirianni recapped the loss to Carolina by saying the offense has to score more points and the team has to clean up its details. He blamed himself and the staff as much as the players, and said the team played hard and tough but made uncharacteristic mistakes. He praised Tanner McKee for battling, protecting the football and making some good throws, including the touchdown to DeVonta Smith. He admitted the run game isn't working the way they want. Being down 19-7 pushed them into a fast, no-huddle approach late, and he said it has worked for them before. He said the staff will do 'different things' to get the offense going, and that repeating the same approach without results would be foolish. He pointed to three-and-outs and early second-half drives that didn't sustain as the reason the defense played 74 snaps. He acknowledged busted coverages and miscommunication on defense and said he would review the tape. He also said the team has special-teams penalties to clean up. On the four-game losing streak, he said there is always urgency but the team will stay calm and lean on its core values.

title: Todd Bowles on Final Score vs. Steelers | Press Conference
headline: Jalon Daniels is starting for the Bucs while Baker Mayfield's availability is unresolved until Wednesday, and the offense stalled late (34 second-half yards) in the overtime loss to Pittsburgh.
summary: Bowles was frustrated after a loss in which Tampa Bay blew a 13-point fourth-quarter lead and lost in overtime. He said the team played hard but has to learn to finish games in all three phases, with 'no more margin for error.' He blamed missed tackles, including on checkdowns, and one late jump off the ball for the defensive collapse. He defended Jalon Daniels, who threw two late interceptions, as having played hard, and said the turnovers were a team issue. He said he'd have to watch the tape to judge whether the picks came from inaccuracy, a bad route or pressure. On Mayfield, he said he saw 'not much' from him this week and will have a better answer Wednesday. He said Mayfield is not ruled out for next week and that he just needs to see more. He said Bucky Irving struggled against a tough front, lacked last week's rhythm, and was often stuck in second-and-long. He rejected the idea that the team lacks a No. 1 receiver, saying it should change every game. He took responsibility for the play-calling, saying all of the play-calling needs to be better, and pointed to poor third-down execution.

topics.detail: Bowles repeatedly said the team must finish games in all three phases after losing a 13-point fourth-quarter lead. He pointed to missed tackles on checkdowns and a late jump off the ball, and said the locker room won't break.
Asked about the pass-rush success of David Walker, Rueben Bain and others, Bowles said he judges success by wins and losses, not pressure. He said closing out games is a team responsibility.

Bowles explained the first-play interior run in overtime as an attempt to get a positive play and see if they could pop one through. He said he was unhappy with all of the play-calling, including his own, and that the offense failed to convert third downs.

Bowles said the team doesn't lack a No. 1 receiver and that the top target 'should change every game.' He said a deep-ball miss near the end zone was a hard one-handed reach, not a sign of miscommunication.
Bowles said he didn't think Pittsburgh specifically targeted Jacob Parrish, though he questioned a pass interference call against him.
